image_description: A top-down view of a chiton (polyplacophore) clinging to a surface. The organism displays an elongated oval shape with a distinct dorsal armor consisting of eight overlapping calcareous plates arranged in a linear series. These plates are greyish-green with vertical striations and are surrounded by a dark brown, textured leathery girdle (mantle). The head region is indistinct and blunt, lacking visible eyes or tentacles.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Exactly eight distinct plate segments are visible running from anterior to posterior, overlapping slightly at the joints, which is the defining characteristic of a chiton.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Can curl into defensive ball when dislodged.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a behavioral capability, not a static visual feature present in a single image of an attached specimen.
